title: The likelihood of a bushing fleet's history

blocks.text: A transmission company is fitting a Weibull curve to the history of one kind of transformer bushing. For each bushing that failed it knows the age at failure; for each bushing still in service it knows only its age today. The fitting routine maximizes a log-likelihood over `beta` and `eta`, and you are writing that function.
Write `log_likelihood(beta, eta, failed, working)` in `likelihood.py`: `failed` is the list of failure ages, `working` the list of current ages of the bushings still in service, all in years.

Write the formula in the lesson's notation first, a sum over failed units and a sum over units still working, then expand $`\ln f(t)`$ and $`\ln R(c)`$ for the Weibull so that you need only `math.log` and powers. The tests compare your value with `scipy.stats.weibull_min`'s `logpdf` and `logsf`. About six lines.

cases.says: when every unit has failed, the log-likelihood is the sum of the log densities at the failure ages
a unit still in service adds the log of the probability of lasting to its current age
with many units still working, the curve that lets them last scores higher than one fitted to early failures
